Parameter sweeps and Monte Carlo experiments

Source: R/sweep.R
sim_sweep.Rd

sim_sweep() runs one simulation per row of parameters, a data frame (or list of named lists) of model parameter values. The model is compiled once; each run uses sim_set_params(), which reuses the dependency analysis whenever the structure is unchanged.

sim_sweep(
  x,
  parameters,
  tspan,
  times = NULL,
  summary = NULL,
  keep = TRUE,
  cores = 1,
  ...
)

sim_monte_carlo(
  x,
  n,
  sampler,
  seed,
  tspan,
  times = NULL,
  summary = NULL,
  keep = TRUE,
  cores = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A sim_model() or a compiled sim_plan.

parameters

Data frame of parameter values, one run per row, or a list of named lists.

tspan, times

Passed to sim_run().

summary

Optional function of a sim_result returning a named numeric vector. Its values are collected in $summary.

keep

Keep the full results (TRUE) or only the summaries.

cores

Number of parallel workers.

...

Further arguments for sim_run().

n

Number of Monte Carlo runs.

sampler

Function of the run index returning a named list of parameter values.

seed

Integer seed for sampler.

Value

A sim_sweep object with elements parameters, results (when keep = TRUE), status and summary (a data frame of parameters and summary values).

Details

sim_monte_carlo() draws n parameter sets with sampler(i) under a fixed seed and runs them like a sweep. The caller's random number stream is saved and restored, so the experiment is reproducible and does not disturb the global random state.

With cores > 1 runs use parallel::mclapply() (not available on Windows, where runs are sequential). Results do not depend on cores.

Examples

m <- sim_model("decay", params = list(a = 1))
sim_add_block(m, "integrator", "x", initial = 1)
sim_add_block(m, "gain", "k", gain = sim_param("a"))
sim_add_block(m, "gain", "neg", gain = -1)
sim_connect(m, "x", "k")
sim_connect(m, "k", "neg")
sim_connect(m, "neg", "x")
s <- sim_sweep(m, data.frame(a = c(0.5, 1, 2)), tspan = c(0, 1),
  summary = function(r) c(x_end = tail(sim_signal(r, "x"), 1)))
s$summary
#>     a     x_end  status
#> 1 0.5 0.6065307 success
#> 2 1.0 0.3678794 success
#> 3 2.0 0.1353353 success
mc <- sim_monte_carlo(m, n = 5, sampler = function(i) list(a = runif(1, 0, 2)),
  seed = 42, tspan = c(0, 1), keep = FALSE,
  summary = function(r) c(x_end = tail(sim_signal(r, "x"), 1)))
mc$summary
#>           a     x_end  status
#> 1 1.8296121 0.1604758 success
#> 2 1.8741508 0.1534852 success
#> 3 0.5722791 0.5642380 success
#> 4 1.6608953 0.1899688 success
#> 5 1.2834910 0.2770683 success
